title: Pisces Moon:
all about you.
summary: What Vedic astrology reads in a Pisces Moon: Jupiter, water, the gift and the catch, love, work, and the three birth stars inside the sign.
imageAlt: Maya holding a Pisces flag, with two fish in a bubble of water beside her
inside: Jupiter, water and the dual quality, and what each is read to give you
The gift and the catch, then love, work, money and energy
The three birth stars inside Pisces, in a table you can look yourself up in
Five things to do with a Pisces Moon
intro: If the Moon was in Pisces when you were born, Vedic astrology reads you as the one who feels what everyone else is feeling. Gentle, imaginative, forgiving, and quick to show up when someone is hurting. The film says that in sixty seconds. This guide takes the long way round: where that nature is said to come from, what it is good for, where it wears you out, and how the tradition tells one Pisces Moon from another.

A note before you start. Everything here is what the tradition reads from the sign, said as a tendency and never as a rule. Your Moon sign is one part of a chart, and the rest of your chart, your upbringing and your own choices all shape how much of this you recognise.

sections.label: What you are made of
title: Jupiter, water,
and a sign that flows.
paragraphs: Every sign has a ruler, an element and a quality. For Pisces those are Jupiter, water and dual. Together they explain almost everything said about the sign.

Pisces is the twelfth and last of the signs, and its symbol is two fish swimming in opposite directions. The tradition reads the last sign as the place where the zodiac lets go: of borders, of keeping score, of the line between me and you. The two fish are one foot in this world and one in the world of dreams.

items.name: The ruler: Jupiter
items.text: Jupiter is the guru, the teacher among the planets: wisdom, faith, kindness and growth. Jupiter rules two signs, Sagittarius and Pisces. In Sagittarius that wisdom goes out into the world as belief and adventure; in Pisces it turns inward, as compassion and a quiet trust that things work out. A Pisces Moon is read as someone who keeps the faith, in people and in life, even on hard days.

items.name: The element: water
items.text: Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces are the three water signs. Water is read as feeling, intuition and care. In Pisces it is the open sea: wide, deep, and able to take in almost anything. That is why this Moon is said to pick up moods in a room before anyone says a word.

items.name: The quality: dual
items.text: Signs are movable, fixed or dual. Pisces is dual, along with Gemini, Virgo and Sagittarius. Dual signs are read as adaptable: they bend, see both sides and change with the situation. In Pisces this shows as a gift for understanding anyone, and a habit of becoming a little like whoever you are with.

sections.label: The gift and the catch
title: Compassion first,
boundaries second.
paragraphs: The gift is compassion. A Pisces Moon is read as the friend who notices you are not fine, who sits with you without needing to fix it, and who is already holding the tissues before you start to cry. You tend to forgive quickly and remember the good in people long after others have given up on them. People leave time with you feeling softer and less alone.

The catch is boundaries. The same open water that takes in other people's feelings can take in too much of them. The tradition reads this Moon as soaking up everyone's worries, saying yes when it means no, and then needing a long rest to find itself again. It is not weakness. It is a sea without a shore. The answer the tradition gives is not to feel less, but to build a little shore: a time, a place or a word that is yours alone.

sections.label: Love
title: A romantic,
who sees the best.
paragraphs: In love a Pisces Moon is said to be the romantic of the zodiac. It loves deeply, gives generously and sees the best in people, sometimes before they have shown it. Venus is said to be exalted in Pisces, at her strongest in this sign, and the tradition reads that as a sign built for tender, devoted love.

items.name: What you bring
items.text: Tenderness, imagination and a deep kind of attention. You tend to remember the small things, write the long message, and make a partner feel understood without having to explain.

items.name: What you need
items.text: Gentleness and steadiness. This Moon is said to bloom with a partner who is kind, calm and honest, and who gives it room to drift into its own world now and then without taking it personally.

items.name: What tends to go wrong
items.text: Seeing someone as they could be rather than as they are, and staying too long out of hope. The fix the tradition suggests is simple: let people show you who they are over time, and trust what they do as much as what you feel.

items.name: Work
items.text: At work a Pisces Moon is read as someone who shines where the work means something. Art, music, writing, film, teaching, healing, counselling and caring for others are the classic fits. You tend to do well where imagination or kindness is the skill, and to struggle in places that are cold, loud or only about numbers.

items.name: With a boss or a team
items.text: You are said to be the one who keeps the peace and notices who is struggling. The risk is quietly taking on other people's work. It helps to write down what is yours, and to ask for clear deadlines so the dreamy side has a frame to work in.

items.name: Money
items.text: In plain terms the tradition reads this Moon as soft with money: lending, giving, paying for someone who is short this month. It says nothing certain about how much money comes your way. The habit that is said to help most is a simple plan made on a calm day, so kindness does not leave you short.

items.name: Energy
items.text: Your energy is read as tidal: high when you feel connected, low after crowds and other people's problems. Sleep, water, music, quiet and time alone tend to refill you. For a Pisces Moon, rest is not a reward for finishing; it is part of the work.

sections.label: Look yourself up
title: The three birth stars
inside Pisces.
paragraphs: The sky is also divided into twenty-seven birth stars, called nakshatras, each 13°20′ wide. Three of them fall inside the thirty degrees of Pisces. Which one your Moon was in is your birth star, and the tradition uses it to tell one Pisces Moon from another. Each star has a ruling planet of its own, which colours Jupiter and water underneath. Your chart shows the degree of your Moon; find it in the left column.

rows.v: Purva Bhadrapada (last quarter), ruled by Jupiter
rows.note: The front of the funeral cot, read as the star of fire and devotion. Only its last quarter is in Pisces; the rest is in Aquarius. Read as the most intense Pisces Moon: idealistic, committed to a cause, and capable of great sacrifice for what it believes. The catch is swinging between extremes.

The back of the cot, the star of the deep. Read as the steadiest Pisces Moon: calm, wise, patient and good in a crisis, with a kindness that stays when others leave. The catch is keeping its own needs hidden for too long.

The drum, the last of all twenty-seven stars and the star of safe journeys. Read as the gentlest Pisces Moon: imaginative, caring, protective of anyone small or lost, and gifted with words and art. The catch is being too trusting.

after: If your Moon sits within a degree of one of these borders, the exact time of birth decides which side it falls on. Revati ends exactly where Pisces ends and Aries begins, the meeting point of water and fire, which the tradition treats with special care. All three are still Pisces, with Jupiter as the sign ruler. The birth star adds a second voice, it does not replace the first.

sections.label: What to do
title: Five habits
for a Pisces Moon.
paragraphs: None of this is about caring less. It is about giving a soft, open nature the shore it needs, so the kindness can keep flowing.

steps.name: Practise one small no
steps.text: Pick one request this week that you would usually say yes to out of guilt, and say a kind no instead. It gets easier every time, and the people who matter will understand.

steps.name: Rest before you are empty
steps.text: Put quiet time in your week the way you would put in a meeting. A Pisces Moon is said to give its best when it has rested first, not after it has run dry.

steps.name: Notice whose feeling it is
steps.text: When a mood comes over you, ask: is this mine, or did I pick it up from someone? Just asking the question tends to loosen its grip.

steps.name: Make something
steps.text: Water under Jupiter wants to turn feeling into something shared. Write, draw, sing, play, cook. Giving the feeling a shape tends to calm it.

steps.name: Let people show you who they are
steps.text: Keep seeing the best in people, and also watch what they do over time. Your hope is a gift; let their actions earn it.

faq.q: Is this for my Sun sign or my Moon sign?
faq.a: Your Moon sign. Vedic astrology reads your nature and your timing from the sign the Moon was in when you were born, which is often different from the Sun sign most people know.

faq.q: I’m a Pisces Sun. Does this apply to me?
faq.a: Only if your Moon is also in Pisces. Many people with a Pisces Sun have their Moon somewhere else, and Vedic signs are counted from the stars, so even your Sun sign may differ. Your birth chart shows your Moon sign in a few seconds.

faq.q: How do I find my birth star?
faq.a: From the degree of your Moon, which your birth chart shows. The Moon moves about thirteen degrees a day, so you need your date, place and time of birth. Draw your chart on the home page and look for the Moon’s sign and degree.

note: Sign rulers, elements, qualities, exaltations and birth stars are those of the classical tradition. Vedic (sidereal) astrology, Lahiri ayanamsa, read by Moon sign.
